name: pymc-bayesian-modeling
capability: priors and likelihoods; NUTS/ADVI; R-hat/ESS/divergence diagnostics; prior/posterior predictive checks; LOO/WAIC comparison; hierarchical/logistic/GP models
primary_issue: Core Bayesian workflow is broadly sound, but fixed d_loo evidence bands and advice to switch from problematic LOO to WAIC are not generally valid; WAIC is not a remedy for influential observations. Pickle loading is unsafe for untrusted artifacts.

name: scikit-survival-analysis
capability: survival data structures; Cox/Coxnet; survival forests/boosting/SVM; Kaplan-Meier/Nelson-Aalen; censoring-aware metrics; competing risks
primary_issue: Strong scope and censoring guidance, but the CIF example destructures the function as three return values although the API returns time plus a cumulative-incidence array. Treating competing events as censored is valid for cause-specific hazards but must not be interpreted as CIF/subdistribution risk. Claims that Uno C is required for any cross-dataset comparison are overbroad.

name: statistical-analysis
capability: test selection; assumption checks; effect sizes; power; multiple testing; reporting; Bayesian overview
primary_issue: Contains material statistical errors: p-values are reduced to P(data|H0), Bayesian methods are said to work with any sample size, and failed normality tests automatically route to rank tests even though these answer different estimands and normality tests are sample-size sensitive. Fixed Durbin-Watson/VIF/event-per-variable rules and blanket Likert/observational claims are not defensible as universal rules.

name: statsmodels-statistical-modeling
capability: OLS/WLS/GLS; GLM; logit/probit/count models; ARIMA/SARIMAX; diagnostics; formula API; power and mixed effects
primary_issue: Useful code patterns, but diagnostic p-value dichotomies and automatic robust-SE fallback oversimplify model misspecification; AIC/BIC and likelihood-ratio comparison require comparable likelihood/data and nested-model conditions not fully stated.

name: cellpose-cell-segmentation
capability: Cellpose 2D/3D cell/nucleus segmentation, measurement, batching and fine-tuning
primary_issue: Overclaims generalization without tuning across bacteria/organoids/stains and says manual parameter tuning is eliminated (11,17).; Parameter table says increasing cellprob_threshold finds more cells (268), while actual examples/troubleshooting use a lower value (-2) for more detections (369); the guidance is internally contradictory.; API/model examples are tied to older Cellpose model names and return shapes without a tested version pin (54-55,100-116,264-273).; No ground-truth sampling, boundary/object metrics, failure-stratum QC or uncertainty gate before morphometry.

name: flowio-flow-cytometry
capability: FCS 2.0-3.1 parse/write, metadata, events and conversion
primary_issue: Recipe recommends dividing fluorescence by PnR for cross-sample comparison (305-321); detector range is not a biological normalization and ignores compensation, transforms, acquisition settings, controls and batch effects.; Best practice says preserve flow.text on re-export (272), which can propagate instrument/sample identifiers and stale acquisition metadata into modified data.; Troubleshooting suggests bypassing offset validation (328-330) without a provenance/corruption warning.; FlowIO is correctly scoped as parser, but downstream ML suggestions need compensation, QC, gating and transformation controls.

name: napari-image-viewer
capability: Interactive multidimensional image, label, point, shape and track viewing plus screenshots
primary_issue: Plugin installs are unpinned and community plugins have separate trust/supply-chain risk (31-42,373-381).; Screenshots and threshold overlays are illustrative; they must not replace blinded/quantitative segmentation validation.; Axis and scale metadata must be explicitly verified for real microscopy files.

name: opencv-bioimage-analysis
capability: Classical CV preprocessing, thresholding, contours, morphology and video
primary_issue: 16-bit scientific images are globally min-max normalized to 8-bit before thresholding (139-144,395-396), making thresholds incomparable across images and discarding intensity calibration.; The 'rolling ball' recipe is a Gaussian blur subtraction, not a rolling-ball algorithm (372-388).; MOG2 moving-contour counts are presented as cell counts without camera/stage drift, photobleaching, focus, object identity or temporal validation (216-251).; Reported contour count includes contours later skipped by area filter in annotation output (357-369).

name: pyimagej-fiji-bridge
capability: Headless/GUI Fiji initialization, macros, Ops, plugins, ROI/results and array conversion
primary_issue: Default initialization downloads a large external runtime on first use (49), so execution requires explicit supply-chain/network approval.; Inline macros and plugin commands depend on global ImageJ state, update sites and command parameter names; static review cannot establish correctness (137-160,213-318).; Axis round trips must be checked against actual TZCYX metadata; a copied array shape is not sufficient proof.; Headless TrackMate recipe is complex and unverified against a pinned TrackMate version (500-568).

name: scikit-image-processing
capability: Scientific image I/O, filtering, segmentation, morphology, measurement and features
primary_issue: Hard-coded CZYX/ZCYX/HWC assumptions (85-94,237-239) require metadata-aware axis validation.; Generic Otsu/watershed/object-size thresholds are illustrative and should be tuned on representative, blinded ground truth (142-174,306-337,394-398).; Co-positive pixels are not equivalent to cell-level co-localization; threshold choice, bleed-through and controls matter (233-239,425-440).

name: trackpy-particle-tracking
capability: Particle detection/linking, drift correction, MSD and diffusion fitting
primary_issue: Claims tp.motion.characterize returns alpha/D_app (232-266), an API not established by the cited Trackpy surface and likely hallucinated/version-specific.; Says linking is a Hungarian bipartite assignment (128-130), an oversimplification of Trackpy subnet/linking behavior.; Best practice says always compute/subtract drift (441), but estimating drift from mobile particles can erase real collective motion; troubleshooting later admits immobile references are required (567), an internal contradiction.; Diffusion fit uses the first ten points with a free intercept and no localization-error, motion-blur, track-length weighting or uncertainty model (205-229).; 3D stack reshape assumes acquisition ordering and dimensions without metadata verification (360-364).

name: matplotlib-scientific-plotting
capability: 2D/3D plots; layouts; styling; export; publication composites
primary_issue: Plotting coverage is useful, but the statistical-comparison workflow fabricates a fixed ** annotation without running any test. That is unsafe scientific code generation and disqualifies the entry as-is.

name: molecular-visualization-3dmol
capability: 3D molecular styles; trajectory animation; normal-mode animation; surfaces; HTML generator
primary_issue: The output is described as self-contained but requires an unpinned live CDN. User-controlled title/subtitle are inserted into HTML without escaping, enabling local HTML/script injection; only structure data is JSON-escaped. Normal-mode visualization is qualitative and lacks unit/provenance checks.

name: multipanel
capability: redraw vs raster composite decision; subfigures/mosaic layout; panel labels; consistent styling; PDF/PNG export
primary_issue: Generally useful layout guidance, but the proprietary declaration alone blocks content adoption. It also calls a PDF containing raster-composited panels a vector output, which can mislead users about editability/resolution.

name: omics-plotting
capability: volcano/MA; heatmaps; GSEA plots; box/violin/bar; PCA/UMAP/t-SNE; Kaplan-Meier
primary_issue: License blocks adoption. The box-plot recipe silently chooses Mann-Whitney for any two groups, computes statistics inside plotting, reports only stars, and ignores pairing/design/estimand; PCA is applied without scaling or missingness/design checks. KM omits risk tables, censoring validation, and inferential context.

name: plotly-interactive-plots
capability: Plotly Express; graph objects; heatmaps; 3D; subplots; HTML/static export; interactive controls
primary_issue: Broad and mostly plausible plotting reference. Simulated volcano/dose-response examples should not be mistaken for inferential workflows, and HTML export needs explicit self-contained/CDN/privacy policy. No critical statistical engine is embedded.

name: scientific-visualization
capability: chart selection; color accessibility; composition; journal formatting; statistical annotation principles
primary_issue: The strongest visualization guide in scope: it emphasizes exact p-values, effects, sample size and CVD-safe palettes. Journal requirements remain mutable and must be checked against the target journal rather than treated as evergreen.

name: seaborn-statistical-plots
capability: distribution/categorical/relational/regression plots; heatmaps/clustermaps; grids; volcano-like workflows
primary_issue: Contains a concrete scientific labeling error: seaborn clustermap standard_scale=0 performs min-max scaling, not z-scoring, yet the comments/colorbar say z-score. Volcano example names a raw p-value threshold padj_thresh, and a simulated RNA/protein correlation plot actually generates independent RNA terms for x and y.

name: statistical-significance-annotation
capability: p-to-star mapping; multiple-testing advice; bracket drawing; seaborn integration
primary_issue: The guide encourages stars and qualitative labels instead of exact adjusted p-values/effect estimates. Its ANOVA example follows an omnibus parametric test with pairwise Mann-Whitney tests without design justification. Helper dh/barh are documented as axes fractions but added directly to data-coordinate y, so placement is dimensionally wrong.

name: bwa-mem2-dna-aligner
capability: Fast short-read DNA aligner for WGS/WES/ChIP-seq. 2× faster BWA-MEM successor; outputs SAM/BAM with read group headers for GATK. Primary plus supplementary records for chimeric reads. Use STAR for RNA-seq splice-aware alignment; Bowtie2 is a comparable alternative.
primary_issue: The workflow hard-codes GRCh38 download/build examples and an unverified 2x/identical-results claim; read group, alt-contig, duplicate, contamination, and reference-bundle choices remain analysis-specific.

name: pysam-genomic-files
capability: Read/write SAM/BAM/CRAM, VCF/BCF, FASTA/FASTQ. Region queries, pileup, variant filtering, read groups. Python htslib wrapper exposing samtools/bcftools CLI. Use STAR/BWA for alignment; GATK/DeepVariant for variant calling.
primary_issue: Recipes expose low-level indexed I/O but do not establish coordinate/build invariants or safe write semantics; pileup/filter behavior is parameter- and htslib-version-dependent.

name: samtools-bam-processing
capability: CLI toolkit for SAM/BAM/CRAM: sort, index, convert, filter, QC alignments. Core commands: view, sort, index, flagstat, stats, depth, markdup, merge. Required between alignment and variant/peak calling. Use pysam for Python-native BAM access; deeptools for normalized coverage tracks.
primary_issue: Command recipes can silently discard records through flag/MAPQ filters or change representation through CRAM conversion; reference identity and provenance must be pinned.

name: star-rna-seq-aligner
capability: Splice-aware RNA-seq aligner producing sorted BAM and splice junction tables. Builds genome index, runs two-pass alignment for better junctions. Outputs sorted BAM, junctions (SJ.out.tab), stats (Log.final.out), optional gene counts. Use Salmon for fast pseudoalignment; STAR when a BAM is needed for variant calling, IGV, or ENCODE pipelines.
primary_issue: Pins STAR/GENCODE examples to a moving release and treats generic two-pass settings as broadly suitable; read length, overhang, multimapping, chimeric reads, and annotation/reference coupling require assay-specific validation.

name: bakta-genome-annotation
capability: Annotate bacterial and archaeal genomes and plasmids with Bakta's Prodigal/HMM/diamond pipeline. Identifies CDS, ncRNA, tRNA, rRNA, tmRNA, sORFs, CRISPR arrays, oriC/oriV/oriT, and gaps against a curated UniRef-derived database. Produces NCBI-compatible GFF3, GenBank, EMBL, JSON, FASTA, TSV, and a circular genome plot. Use Prokka for legacy pipelines or non-bacterial kingdoms; PGAP for NCBI GenBank submission.
primary_issue: Annotation quality depends on the separately downloaded Bakta database release and taxonomic scope; predicted function is not experimentally validated and the prose license is conflated with tool/data licenses.

name: prokka-genome-annotation
capability: Annotate prokaryotic genomes (bacteria, archaea, viruses) via Prokka's BLAST/HMM pipeline. Identifies CDS, rRNA, tRNA, tmRNA, signal peptides against Pfam, TIGRFAMs, RefSeq. Outputs GFF3, GenBank, FASTA, TSV. Use PGAP for NCBI GenBank submission; Bakta for faster NCBI-compatible annotation.
primary_issue: A legacy database/tool chain is presented as a general bacteria/archaea/virus solution; fragmented assemblies and stale reference databases can propagate false or generic product names.

name: roary-pangenome
capability: Compute the bacterial pan-genome from Prokka/Bakta GFF3 annotations with Roary's CD-HIT + BLAST + MCL clustering pipeline. Builds gene presence/absence matrices, core/soft-core/shell/cloud partitions, multi-FASTA core gene alignments (with `-e`), and a pan-genome reference. Use Panaroo for higher-accuracy pan-genomes from highly fragmented assemblies, PIRATE for paralog-aware clustering, or PPanGGOLiN for graph-based partitioning.
primary_issue: Roary clustering is sensitive to annotation consistency, fragmentation, paralogs, identity threshold, and population structure; presence/absence association is not causal and default intermediate cleanup is mutating.

name: arboreto-grn-inference
capability: GRN inference from expression via GRNBoost2 (gradient boosting) or GENIE3 (Random Forest). Load matrix, filter by TFs, infer TF-target-importance links, save network. Dask-parallelized to single-cell scale. Core SCENIC component.
primary_issue: Tree importance from co-expression is association, not directed or causal regulation; stochasticity, TF-list coverage, cell-state confounding, and missing motif validation are not resolved.

name: biopython-molecular-biology
capability: Molecular biology toolkit: sequence manipulation, FASTA/GenBank/PDB I/O, NCBI Entrez, BLAST automation, pairwise/MSA alignment, Bio.PDB, phylogenetic trees. Use for batch processing, custom pipelines, format conversion, PubMed/GenBank queries. For quick gene lookups use gget; for multi-service REST APIs use bioservices.
primary_issue: A broad cookbook mixes local algorithms with remote Entrez/BLAST and external aligners; sequence submission can disclose unpublished data and examples are not version-pinned.

name: biopython-sequence-analysis
capability: Biopython sequence analysis: parse FASTA/FASTQ/GenBank/GFF (SeqIO), NCBI Entrez (esearch/efetch/elink), remote/local BLAST, pairwise/MSA alignment (PairwiseAligner, MUSCLE/ClustalW), phylogenetic trees (Phylo). Use for gene family studies, phylogenomics, comparative genomics, NCBI pipelines. For PCR/restriction/cloning use biopython-molecular-biology; for SAM/BAM use pysam.
primary_issue: Remote Entrez/BLAST plus external MUSCLE/Clustal wrappers introduce network, privacy, executable, and version drift; phylogeny recipes do not establish model adequacy or uncertainty.

name: archs4-database
capability: Query ARCHS4 REST API for uniformly processed RNA-seq expression, tissue patterns, co-expression across 1M+ human/mouse samples. Retrieve z-scores, co-expressed genes, samples by metadata, HDF5 matrices. For variant population genetics use gnomad-database; for pathway enrichment use gget-genomic-databases (Enrichr).
primary_issue: Hard-coded undocumented-looking /api/v1 response schemas and printed numerical outputs are not backed by a snapshot or retrieval evidence; ARCHS4 content and processing versions are mutable.

name: bioservices-multi-database
capability: Unified Python interface to 40+ bioinformatics web services: UniProt proteins, KEGG pathways, ChEMBL/ChEBI/PubChem, BLAST, cross-database ID mapping, GO annotations, PPI. For deep single-DB queries use dedicated tools (gget for Ensembl, pubchempy for PubChem); bioservices excels at cross-database workflows.
primary_issue: A wrapper over many independently changing services includes legacy PICR/old method signatures; cross-database mappings are many-to-many and release-dependent, yet no executable compatibility matrix is proved.

name: cbioportal-database
capability: Cancer genomics (TCGA et al.) via cBioPortal REST API. Retrieve somatic mutations, CNAs, expression, clinical data (survival/stage/treatment) across thousands of studies. Use for TMB, oncoprints, survival analysis. For population frequencies use gnomad-database; for drug-gene interactions use opentargets-database.
primary_issue: Study/profile identifiers and clinical endpoints are mutable; recipes risk denominator/sample-vs-patient errors and unadjusted survival/treatment inference from observational cancer cohorts.

name: clinpgx-database
capability: Query the ClinPGx (formerly PharmGKB) REST API plus the CPIC PostgREST companion API for pharmacogenomic clinical annotations, CPIC/DPWG dosing guidelines, gene-drug pairs, variant-drug associations, FDA/EMA drug labels, and PGx pathways. Two-host architecture: api.clinpgx.org for annotation records, api.cpicpgx.org for genotype→recommendation lookups. No auth. For germline pathogenicity use clinvar-database; for somatic cancer PGx use cosmic-database or opentargets-database; for drug bioactivity use chembl-database-bioactivity.
primary_issue: Genotype-to-prescribing text is clinically actionable but omits diplotype calling, allele-function uncertainty, guideline version/effective date, ancestry, contraindications, and clinician/pharmacist review gates.

name: clinvar-database
capability: Query NCBI ClinVar via E-utilities for variant clinical significance, pathogenicity, disease associations. Search by gene/rsID/condition/review status; returns ClinSig, submitter data, conditions, HGVS. For GWAS use gwas-database; for variant consequence prediction use Ensembl VEP.
primary_issue: Clinical significance is condition-, inheritance-, submitter-, review-date-, transcript-, and assembly-specific; string matching Pathogenic is not a clinical interpretation workflow and conflicting/withdrawn assertions can be mishandled.

name: cosmic-database
capability: Query COSMIC for cancer somatic mutations, gene census, mutational signatures, drug resistance variants. REST API v3.1 supports gene/sample/variant queries; free registration. For germline use clinvar-database; for drug-target data use opentargets-database or chembl-database-bioactivity.
primary_issue: The skill assumes a JSON REST surface at cancer.sanger.ac.uk/cosmic/api and constructs Basic auth from plaintext email/password without locally frozen API documentation; commercial-use terms and credential exposure make it unsuitable.

name: dbsnp-database
capability: Query NCBI dbSNP for SNP records by rsID, gene, or region via E-utilities and Variation Services REST API. Retrieve alleles, MAF, variant class (SNV/indel/MNV), clinical links, cross-DB IDs (ClinVar, dbVar, 1000G). Free; 3 req/sec (10 with key). For clinical pathogenicity use clinvar-database; for population frequencies use gnomad-database.
primary_issue: rsIDs can be merged or withdrawn and frequencies are study/population/build-specific; a dbSNP record or ClinVar link does not establish pathogenicity.

name: depmap-crispr-essentiality
capability: DepMap CRISPR gene effect (Chronos) analysis: sign convention for essentiality, per-gene NaN-safe Spearman correlation, data loading/alignment. For general NaN-safe correlation see nan-safe-correlation; for quality filtering see degenerate-input-filtering.
primary_issue: Chronos gene effect and per-gene correlations are release-, cell-line-, copy-number-, lineage-, and missingness-dependent; correlation does not establish target dependency or therapeutic index.

name: ena-database
capability: ENA REST API for sequences, reads, assemblies, and annotations. Portal API search, Browser API retrieval (XML/FASTA/EMBL), file reports for FASTQ/BAM URLs, taxonomy, cross-refs. For multi-DB Python use bioservices; for NCBI-only use pubmed-database or Biopython Entrez.
primary_issue: Declared license is Unknown and accessions/files/checksums/assemblies are mutable; bulk URLs and sample metadata require provenance capture and human-subject/privacy screening.

name: encode-database
capability: ENCODE Portal REST API for regulatory genomics: TF ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq/DNase-seq peaks, histone marks, and RNA-seq across 1000+ cell types. Search experiments by assay/biosample/target; download BED/bigWig; retrieve SCREEN cCREs by region or gene. Use to annotate variants with regulatory tracks, find open chromatin in a cell type, or fetch peak files for ChIP/ATAC analysis. For regulatory variant scoring use regulomedb-database; for GWAS associations use gwas-database.
primary_issue: Assay, biosample, replicate, audit, preferred-file, assembly, and pipeline-version filters determine validity; broad search recipes can mix incomparable experiments and SCREEN response schemas are not frozen.

name: ensembl-database
capability: Ensembl REST API for gene/transcript/variant annotations in 300+ species. Gene info by symbol/ID, sequence, cross-refs (HGNC, RefSeq, UniProt), regulatory features. For bulk local use pyensembl; for pathways use kegg-database.
primary_issue: Unpinned Ensembl REST defaults make IDs, coordinates, transcripts, sequences, and VEP consequences change across releases; assembly and canonical-transcript assumptions must be explicit.

name: gene-database
capability: NCBI Gene via E-utilities: curated records across 1M+ taxa. Official symbols, aliases, RefSeq IDs, summaries, coordinates, GO, interactions. Use for gene ID resolution and cross-species function queries. For sequences use Ensembl; for expression use geo-database.
primary_issue: NCBI Gene symbols/aliases and cross-species records are not one-to-one; E-utilities results are mutable and summaries are descriptive evidence, not functional or clinical truth.

name: geo-database
capability: NCBI GEO access via GEOparse and E-utilities. Search by keyword/organism/platform, download GSE series matrices, parse GPL annotations, extract GSM metadata, load expression matrices into pandas. For single-cell use cellxgene-census; for multi-DB access use gget-genomic-databases.
primary_issue: GEO matrices are heterogeneous in normalization/platform and sample labels; generic extraction cannot support DE without study-specific design/QC, and patient metadata may be sensitive despite public hosting.

name: gget-genomic-databases
capability: Unified CLI/Python interface to 20+ genomic databases. Gene lookups (Ensembl search/info/seq), BLAST/BLAT, AlphaFold, Enrichr enrichment, OpenTargets disease/drug, CELLxGENE single-cell, cBioPortal/COSMIC cancer, ARCHS4 expression. Spans genomics, proteomics, disease. For batch/advanced BLAST use biopython; for multi-DB Python SDK use bioservices.
primary_issue: One skill spans many mutable services and optional local executables; ancillary text internally labels AlphaFold access as a local ColabFold/OpenMM model and includes COSMIC passwords, so version/API/provenance boundaries are not trustworthy.

name: gnomad-database
capability: gnomAD v4 population variant frequencies via GraphQL API. Allele counts and frequencies stratified by ancestry (AFR, AMR, EAS, NFE, SAS, FIN, ASJ, MID), gene-level constraint (pLI, LOEUF, missense z), and coverage. Identify rare or constrained variants. For clinical pathogenicity use clinvar-database; for GWAS use gwas-database.
primary_issue: The quick start labels BRCA1 pLI about 5.5e-38 as very high LoF intolerance even though pLI ranges 0-1 and that value is near zero; population frequency/constraint is not pathogenicity evidence.

name: gwas-database
capability: NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog REST API for SNP-trait associations from published GWAS. Query studies, associations, variants, traits, genes, summary stats. Build PRS candidates, analyze pleiotropy, fetch stats for Manhattan plots. No auth.
primary_issue: Catalog associations are ancestry-, LD-, phenotype-, build-, and publication-dependent and are not causal; PRS construction needs harmonization, effect alleles, ancestry calibration, and external validation absent here.

name: jaspar-database
capability: JASPAR 2024 TF binding profiles via REST API and pyJASPAR. Retrieve PFMs/PWMs by TF name, JASPAR ID, species, or structural class. Scan DNA for TFBS; browse by taxon (human, mouse) or TF family (bHLH, zinc finger). Use for motif enrichment input, TFBS scanning, and regulatory sequence analysis. For ChIP-seq peak motif discovery use homer-motif-analysis; for regulatory variant scoring use regulomedb-database.
primary_issue: The code treats JASPAR PFM as position-keyed although API PFMs are base-keyed arrays, computes maximum score by summing all positive bases rather than per-position maxima, and scans only the forward strand.

name: kegg-database
declared_license: Non-academic use of KEGG requires a commercial license
capability: KEGG REST API (academic only). Pathways, genes, compounds, enzymes, diseases, drugs via 7 ops (info/list/find/get/conv/link/ddi). ID conversion (NCBI/UniProt/PubChem). Use bioservices for multi-DB Python.
primary_issue: KEGG permits academic REST use but non-academic redistribution/use may require a commercial license; records are mutable and pathway membership does not establish mechanism or enrichment significance.

name: monarch-database
capability: Monarch Initiative knowledge graph REST API for disease-gene-phenotype associations and cross-species orthology. MONDO disease-to-gene/phenotype, HP phenotype profiles, cross-species comparisons. Use for rare disease gene prioritization and phenotype-based candidate ranking. For GWAS use gwas-database; for clinical pathogenicity use clinvar-database.
primary_issue: Aggregated disease-gene-phenotype edges differ in evidence type and model organism; phenotype matching is prioritization, not diagnosis, and API/ontology versions are not pinned.

name: mouse-phenome-database
capability: Retrieve mouse phenotype data from the Jackson Laboratory Mouse Phenome Database (MPD) via its REST API. Browse 520+ projects, look up per-project measure metadata, pull strain-level means (raw or LS-mean adjusted) and per-animal values, find measures by MP/VT ontology terms, and resolve strain nomenclature or gene coordinates. Use for QTL support, cross-strain comparison, mouse model selection, and ontology-driven phenotype discovery. Use monarch-database for disease-gene-phenotype knowledge graphs; ensembl-database for mouse genome annotations.
primary_issue: Project-scoped measures require sex, age, diet, strain, batch, and study-design context; cross-project means and ontology matches are not directly comparable or causal.

name: quickgo-database
capability: Query EBI QuickGO REST API for GO terms and protein annotations. Fetch term metadata by ID, search by keyword, walk ancestor/descendant hierarchies, download annotations filtered by taxon, evidence code, aspect. Use for GO resolution, ontology traversal, annotation retrieval before enrichment. Use gseapy-gene-enrichment for enrichment; uniprot-protein-database for proteins.
primary_issue: GO annotations must retain evidence code, qualifier, taxon, date, and ontology release; electronic and experimental annotations cannot be pooled as equivalent biological proof.

name: regulomedb-database
capability: Query RegulomeDB v2 GET REST API to score variants for regulatory function and retrieve overlapping evidence (TF binding, histone marks, DNase peaks, footprints, motifs, eQTLs, chromatin state). Scores range 1a (strongest) to 7 (none). Use for GWAS hit prioritization, regulatory variant annotation, cis-regulatory discovery. Use clinvar-database for pathogenicity; gwas-database for trait associations.
primary_issue: A mutable web endpoint and assumed JSON schema are used as an API; scores/ranks are functional-prioritization evidence, not pathogenicity, causality, or tissue-matched validation.

name: remap-database
capability: Query ReMap 2022 TF ChIP-seq peak database via REST API and BED downloads. Retrieve TF peaks overlapping a region (chr:start-end), peaks near a gene, TFs by species, peaks filtered by biotype (promoter, enhancer), and BED files for a TF-cell type pair. Use for TF co-occupancy, regulatory annotation, and TF binding atlases. Use jaspar-database for PWM motifs; encode-database for ENCODE tracks.
primary_issue: A static 2022 ChIP-seq atlas is queried through an assumed API schema; assembly, antibody, cell context, peak quality, blacklist, and experiment redundancy determine whether overlap is meaningful.

name: ucsc-genome-browser
capability: Query UCSC Genome Browser REST API for DNA sequences, tracks, gene models, and conservation across 100+ assemblies. Retrieve sequence by region, list/fetch BED/bigWig tracks, chromosome sizes, RefSeq/GENCODE gene structures, PhyloP/PhastCons scores. Use for UCSC annotations; Ensembl REST API for Ensembl gene IDs and VEP variant annotation.
primary_issue: UCSC coordinates are 0-based half-open while many genomic conventions differ; assembly/track version and table schema are mutable, making silent off-by-one or build mismatch likely.

name: etetoolkit
capability: ETE Toolkit (ETE3): Python phylogenetic tree analysis and visualization. Parse Newick/NHX/PhyloXML, traverse/annotate nodes, render figures with TreeStyle/NodeStyle, integrate NCBI taxonomy, run PhyloTree comparative genomics. Use for species trees, gene family evolution, annotated tree figures.
primary_issue: Tree rendering/manipulation is useful but NCBI taxonomy is network/version dependent and topology alone lacks model support, rooting, branch uncertainty, and orthology validation.

name: homer-motif-analysis
capability: De novo and known TF motif enrichment in ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq peaks via HOMER. findMotifsGenome.pl finds over-represented patterns vs background; annotatePeaks.pl assigns context (TSS distance, gene, repeat). Use after MACS3 to identify enriched TFs, annotate peaks with nearest genes, and validate ChIP-seq via the target motif.
primary_issue: Motif enrichment is dominated by background construction, GC/length bias, peak quality, motif redundancy, and genome build; motif presence is not TF binding or regulation.

name: bedtools-genomic-intervals
capability: Genomic interval ops on BED/BAM/GFF/VCF. Find overlaps, merge intervals, compute coverage, extract FASTA, find nearest features. Core for ChIP-seq peak annotation, region filtering, genome arithmetic. Use tabix for indexed single-region queries; use deeptools for normalized bigWig coverage.
primary_issue: Correctness depends on 0-based/1-based conventions, half-open intervals, sort order, strand, assembly, contig naming, and treatment of split reads; generic commands can silently produce plausible wrong overlaps.

name: deeptools-ngs-analysis
capability: NGS CLI for ChIP/RNA/ATAC-seq. BAM→bigWig with RPGC/CPM/RPKM, sample correlation/PCA, heatmaps/profiles around features, fingerprints. For alignment use STAR/BWA; for peak calling use MACS2.
primary_issue: CPM/RPKM/RPGC normalization and visualization depend on effective genome size, excluded regions, duplicates, depth, assay, and controls; heatmaps/correlation are not inferential validation.

name: geniml
capability: Python library for genomic interval ML. Train/apply region2vec embeddings turning BED regions into vectors, index interval datasets for ML, search embedding space with BEDSpace, and evaluate embedding quality. Use for chromatin accessibility clustering, regulatory element classification, and cross-sample region comparison.
primary_issue: Embeddings depend on genome build, token universe, training corpus, random seed, negative sampling, and model version; proximity in embedding space is not biological equivalence.

name: gtars
capability: Rust-backed Python library for fast genomic token arithmetic and BED processing. High-performance BED I/O, interval set ops (intersect, merge, complement, subtract), region tokenization against a universe, universe construction. Use for preprocessing large BED collections and ML token vocabularies.
primary_issue: Fast interval/token operations remain sensitive to build, coordinate convention, universe construction and tokenizer version; performance claims are not locally benchmarked.

name: macs3-peak-calling
capability: Poisson-model peak caller for ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq BAMs. MACS3 callpeak finds enriched regions (TF sites or histone marks) vs input/IgG; outputs BED narrowPeak/broadPeak for motif analysis, annotation, and differential binding. Use narrow peaks for TF ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq; broad for H3K27me3, H3K9me3, and other broad marks.
primary_issue: Peak calls depend on assay-specific shift/extsize, effective genome size, duplicates, controls, blacklist and replicate reproducibility; Poisson enrichment alone is not a validated regulatory site.

name: busco-status-interpretation
capability: Guide to interpreting BUSCO completeness statuses: why Duplicated BUSCOs count as complete, parsing output files, computing/comparing completeness across proteomes/genomes, common counting mistakes. Use when running BUSCO QC, comparing assemblies, or reporting completeness. See also: prokka-genome-annotation for annotation workflows feeding BUSCO.
primary_issue: Duplicated BUSCOs count as complete by definition but may indicate haplotigs, contamination, polyploidy or assembly artifacts; lineage dataset name/version and expected biology must accompany scores.

name: fastp-fastq-preprocessing
capability: All-in-one FASTQ QC and adapter trimming. Auto-detects Illumina adapters, filters low-quality reads, corrects paired-end overlaps, emits HTML+JSON QC in one pass. 3-10x faster than Trim Galore/Trimmomatic. First step before STAR, BWA-MEM2, or Salmon.
primary_issue: Automatic adapter detection and generic quality trimming can remove biological sequence or bias short/low-complexity libraries; before/after QC and assay-specific parameters are required.

name: multiqc-qc-reports
capability: Aggregates QC from 150+ bioinformatics tools into one interactive HTML report. Scans FastQC, samtools, STAR, HISAT2, Trim Galore, featureCounts, Kallisto, Salmon, Picard, GATK logs; merges per-sample stats with plots. For NGS pipeline-wide QC. Use FastQC directly for single-sample; MultiQC for multi-sample reporting.
primary_issue: MultiQC aggregates tool logs but does not validate samples or define pass/fail; HTML can expose sample identifiers and paths, and parser results depend on tool/MultiQC versions.

name: deseq2-differential-expression
capability: Bulk RNA-seq DE with R/Bioconductor DESeq2. Negative binomial GLM, empirical Bayes shrinkage, Wald/LRT tests, multi-factor designs, Salmon tximeta import, apeglm LFC shrinkage, MA/volcano/heatmap viz. R gold standard. Use pydeseq2-differential-expression for Python; use edgeR for TMM normalization.
primary_issue: Negative-binomial inference requires biological replication, correct design/contrast and confounder handling; a fixed count filter/LFC cutoff is not universal and tximeta may fetch mutable metadata.

name: featurecounts-rna-counting
capability: Counts RNA-seq reads overlapping GTF gene features. Takes sorted STAR BAMs plus GTF; outputs a per-gene tab-delimited matrix across samples. Handles strandedness (0/1/2), paired-end, multi-sample batch counting in one command, and outputs assignment statistics. Use Salmon for alignment-free quantification; use featureCounts when STAR BAMs already exist.
primary_issue: Selecting strandedness by whichever mode assigns most reads is not a valid protocol check, and calling most polyA libraries unstranded is unsafe; annotation, multimappers, overlaps and paired-fragment semantics matter.

name: gseapy-gene-enrichment
capability: GSEA and over-representation analysis (ORA) for RNA-seq and proteomics. Wraps Enrichr for ORA against MSigDB, KEGG, GO, and 200+ databases; runs preranked GSEA on ranked DE gene lists. Outputs enrichment tables and running-score plots. Use after DESeq2 or edgeR for pathway-level interpretation.
primary_issue: Remote Enrichr libraries change over time; ORA needs an explicit measured-gene universe and GSEA needs ranked statistics, identifier/species checks and multiple-testing-aware interpretation.

name: pydeseq2-differential-expression
capability: Bulk RNA-seq DE with PyDESeq2: load counts, normalize, fit negative binomial models, Wald test (BH-FDR), LFC shrinkage, volcano/MA plots. Use for two-group comparisons, multi-factor designs with batch correction, multiple contrasts.
primary_issue: PyDESeq2 feature/version parity with DESeq2 is not established and examples assume adequate replication/design; shrinkage, contrasts, Cook filtering and fixed thresholds require validation.

name: salmon-rna-quantification
capability: Ultra-fast RNA-seq transcript/gene quantification via quasi-mapping (no BAM). Builds a k-mer index from transcriptome FASTA, quantifies in minutes. Outputs TPM/count tables (quant.sf) with optional GC- and sequence-bias correction. Integrates with tximeta/tximport for DESeq2/edgeR. Use STAR when a genome-aligned BAM is needed.
primary_issue: Transcript-only and decoy-aware indexes are presented side-by-side without enforcing matching genome/annotation provenance; library type, bias options and gene summarization materially change results.

name: scikit-bio
capability: Python library for biology: sequence manipulation (DNA/RNA/protein), pairwise/multiple alignment, phylogenetic trees (NJ, UPGMA), diversity (Shannon, Faith PD, Bray-Curtis, UniFrac), ordination (PCoA, CCA, RDA), stats (PERMANOVA, ANOSIM, Mantel), file I/O (FASTA, FASTQ, Newick, BIOM). Use for microbiome, community ecology, or phylogenetics.
primary_issue: The broad API cookbook includes version-sensitive/deprecated alignment functions and no DOI citations; distance tests and ordinations require assumptions, permutations and sampling design not guaranteed by snippets.

name: anndata-data-structure
capability: Annotated matrices for single-cell genomics. Stores X with obs/var metadata, layers, embeddings (obsm/varm), graphs (obsp/varp), uns. Use for .h5ad/.zarr I/O, concatenation, scverse integration. For analysis use scanpy; for probabilistic models use scvi-tools.
primary_issue: Recipes mutate or overwrite H5AD/Zarr outputs and can densify huge matrices; raw-count, normalized, layer, gene-identity and backed-mode semantics need explicit invariants and privacy controls.

name: celltypist-cell-annotation
capability: Automated scRNA-seq cell type annotation via pre-trained logistic regression. 45+ models: immune, gut, lung, brain, fetal, cancer microenvironments. Input normalized AnnData; outputs per-cell labels, majority-vote cluster labels, confidence scores. Use for fast, reference-backed annotation without manual marker inspection.
primary_issue: Pretrained labels are reference/model-version dependent and confidence is not calibrated for unseen tissues/disease states; downloaded pickle models and cell-level labels need provenance and manual validation.

name: cellxgene-census
capability: Query CELLxGENE Census (61M+ cells). Search by cell type/tissue/disease/organism; get AnnData, stream out-of-core, train PyTorch models. For your own data use scanpy; for annotated data use anndata.
primary_issue: Census schemas and stable/latest snapshots change; cross-study cells retain batch/protocol/consent limitations, and large local H5AD exports can contain donor/disease metadata.

name: harmony-batch-correction
capability: Harmony batch correction for scRNA-seq and other omics. Removes batch effects from PCA embeddings while preserving biology. Run after PCA, before UMAP. Scales to millions of cells. Python (harmonypy, scanpy) and R (Seurat).
primary_issue: The claim that Harmony removes batch while preserving biology is not guaranteed when batch and biology are confounded; overcorrection must be tested with held-out biology and uncorrected views.

name: popv-cell-annotation
capability: Consensus cell type annotation: runs 10+ algorithms (KNN-Harmony/BBKNN/Scanorama/scVI, CellTypist, ONCLASS, Random Forest, SCANVI, SVM, XGBoost) on a labeled reference and transfers labels via majority voting. Outputs per-method labels, consensus, agreement score. Use when single-method annotation is insufficient or you need ensemble uncertainty for novel states.
primary_issue: Majority voting among correlated methods is not independent evidence or calibrated uncertainty; reference label quality, gene overlap and out-of-distribution cells govern validity.

name: scanpy-scrna-seq
capability: scRNA-seq with Scanpy: QC, normalization, HVG selection, PCA, neighborhood graph, UMAP/t-SNE, Leiden clustering, markers, cell annotation, trajectory inference. Standard scRNA-seq exploration.
primary_issue: The standard workflow uses fixed 200/5000/20% QC cutoffs, treats high gene count as doublets, regresses counts/mitochondrial fraction, and omits required dataset-specific doublet/ambient-RNA validation.

name: scvi-tools-single-cell
capability: Deep generative models for single-cell omics: probabilistic batch correction (scVI), semi-supervised annotation (scANVI), CITE-seq RNA+protein (totalVI), transfer learning (scARCHES), and DE with uncertainty. Unified setup→train→extract API on AnnData. Use harmony-batch-correction for fast linear correction without deep learning; muon for multi-modal MuData workflows.
primary_issue: Deep models are stochastic and can overcorrect confounded biology; architecture/training/version/seed and count-layer assumptions must be pinned, and examples overwrite saved models.

name: single-cell-annotation-guide
capability: Decision framework for manual marker-based, automated (CellTypist), and reference-based (popV) cell type annotation in scRNA-seq. Three-tier strategy: Tier 1 manual markers, Tier 2 CellTypist, Tier 3 popV ensemble transfer. Use when planning or troubleshooting annotation.
primary_issue: The guide correctly warns about high-stakes claims but its three tiers are not independent evidence and cannot replace tissue-specific references, doublet/ambient-RNA QC, ontology mapping and expert adjudication.

name: bcftools-variant-manipulation
capability: CLI for VCF/BCF: filter, merge, annotate, query, normalize, compute stats. Core post-variant-calling: quality filtering, multi-sample merging, rsID annotation, genotype extraction. Samtools companion in HTSlib. Use GATK for complex indel realignment during calling; use VCFtools for population genetics stats.
primary_issue: Commands such as norm -d any delete duplicate records and filters can change cohort/genotype content; reference/build, left-normalization and provenance must be explicit before clinical or population use.

name: cnvkit-copy-number
capability: Detect somatic CNVs from WES/WGS/targeted BAMs (CNVkit v0.9.x). Bin coverage in target/antitarget regions, normalize vs reference, segment with CBS/HMM, call amps/dels, scatter/diagram plots, purity/ploidy, VCF/SEG export. CLI plus Python API (cnvlib). Use GATK CNV for deep WGS with population controls; use CNVkit for targeted/exome where antitarget bins matter.
primary_issue: Copy-number calls depend on purity, ploidy, sex chromosomes, capture design, matched normals and segmentation; export to clinical formats does not make thresholds clinically validated.

name: gatk-variant-calling
capability: GATK Best Practices for germline SNP/indel calling from WGS/WES BAMs. Per-sample HaplotypeCaller GVCFs, GenomicsDBImport, GenotypeGVCFs joint calling, VQSR or hard filters. Requires BWA-MEM2-aligned, markdup, BQSR BAMs. Use DeepVariant for a faster DL alternative; GATK is the NIH/ENCODE standard.
primary_issue: A generic Best Practices sketch hard-codes old dbSNP/resource examples and calls GATK an NIH/ENCODE clinical standard without provenance; assay, pedigree, ploidy, contamination and validation remain unresolved.

name: plink2-gwas-analysis
capability: GWAS and population genetics tool. Processes PLINK (.bed/.bim/.fam), VCF, and BGEN; runs QC (MAF, HWE, missingness), IBD estimation, PCA, and linear/logistic regression GWAS. Outputs Manhattan-ready summary stats. Use regenie or SAIGE for biobanks (>100k samples) needing mixed models.
primary_issue: GWAS requires phenotype/covariate QC, ancestry-aware structure, relatedness, imputation INFO, case/control-specific HWE decisions and privacy safeguards; generic thresholds are not universal.

name: snpeff-variant-annotation
capability: Annotate and filter VCF variants with SnpEff and SnpSift. SnpEff predicts functional effects (HIGH/MODERATE/LOW/MODIFIER), genes, transcripts, AA changes, HGVS; SnpSift filters and adds ClinVar/dbSNP. Java CLI with Python subprocess integration. Use ANNOVAR for multi-database annotation; Ensembl VEP for REST API; SnpEff for fast CLI with pre-built genomes.
primary_issue: HIGH predicted molecular consequence is not pathogenicity or clinical relevance; transcript/build/database choice, HGVS validation, inheritance and phenotype evidence are required.

name: vcf-variant-filtering
capability: Guide to quality filtering raw VCF files before computing summary stats (Ts/Tv ratio, variant counts, AF distributions). Covers detecting raw VCFs via FILTER column and QUAL inspection, QUAL-based filtering with bcftools, Ts/Tv interpretation, and when NOT to filter. Read before any variant-level QC task. See bcftools-variant-manipulation for advanced filters, gatk-variant-calling for caller config, samtools-bam-processing for upstream alignment QC.
primary_issue: QUAL is caller/model-specific evidence against the reference hypothesis, not a universal per-call error probability; blanket QUAL>=30 and fixed Ts/Tv targets can discard truth or retain artifacts.

name: benchling-integration
capability: Benchling registry/inventory/ELN/workflow CRUD and bulk import/export
primary_issue: Contains direct create/update/archive/transfer operations (72-130,158-243) without dry-run, preview, idempotency, approval or readback gates.; Batch archive selects all custom entities older than one year and archives them (465-486), a dangerous policy unrelated to scientific validity.; Exports sequences/inventory without data-classification or PHI/confidentiality controls (358-387,428-448).; Credential storage uses environment variables appropriately (31-55,412), but least-privilege/scopes and secret-redaction are absent.

name: opentrons-protocol-api
capability: OT-2/Flex liquid handling, modules, PCR, dilution and bead cleanup
primary_issue: Simulation is treated as sufficient pre-run validation (509-527), but it cannot validate labware geometry, calibration, liquid class, viscosity, dead volume, deck clearance, contamination, reagent compatibility or biological protocol.; PCR and bead-cleanup temperatures/volumes/cycles are executable defaults without assay validation or operator sign-off (362-425,588-620).; Multi-channel examples conflate one physical 8-tip pickup with 'one tip' and pass whole columns/list shapes in ways requiring device-specific validation (557-578).; No emergency-stop, hazard, aerosol, biosecurity, contamination zoning, waste compatibility or physical supervision gate.

name: protocolsio-integration
capability: Search/retrieve protocols.io protocols, materials, steps, versions and DOIs
primary_issue: Claims sorting by views identifies well-validated protocols because many groups tested them (366); views do not prove execution, reproducibility, safety or quality.; Directly pairs downloaded steps with automation (301-350,440) without human protocol translation, unit normalization, hazard review, equipment equivalence or pilot validation.; Claims all public protocols default to CC-BY-4.0 while simultaneously saying to check individual licenses (370), an internal licensing contradiction.; Quick start encourages literal Bearer placeholder and does not demonstrate environment-secret handling (39-43).

name: pylabrobot
capability: Vendor-agnostic Hamilton/Tecan/Opentrons liquid handling and simulation
primary_issue: Claims one script runs unchanged across vendors (11) despite resource definitions, backends, deck geometry, liquid classes and firmware differences.; Direct physical STAR connection appears immediately after simulator setup (88-94) without an explicit operator approval boundary.; Simulation plus volume/tip checks (354-368) omit calibration, collision, labware, liquid, contamination, waste and hazard validation.; Cherry-pick CSV can drive physical source/destination actions without schema bounds, sample identity readback or two-person verification (301-337).

name: western-blot-quantification
capability: Band ROI detection, normalization, replicate aggregation and visualization
primary_issue: Defines PSMAD2_target = PSMAD2/(SMAD2/GAPDH), which equals PSMAD2*GAPDH/SMAD2 and reintroduces the loading control rather than estimating phospho/total (39,59-60,134-146,302-316).; Suggests excluding an outlier merely for high variability/transfer artifact before specifying a predeclared criterion (83,247); later caveats do not repair selection bias.; Calls n=3 a minimum for meaningful statistics and gives fixed n=4-6 advice without power analysis (78,186,341-342).; Undefined ROI tools make the workflow non-self-contained (92-102).

name: histolab-wsi-processing
capability: WSI tissue masks, filters, tile extraction, QC and visualization
primary_issue: Use only for research preprocessing after slide-level de-identification, annotation provenance and pathologist QC.; Bundled resources openly describe condensation/omission and uncertain APIs (512-545; references/visualization_slides.md:452), so they are not an exhaustive source of truth.; No external holdout, stain/domain-shift or tile-leakage guidance for downstream ML.

name: imaging-data-commons
capability: Local IDC index queries, public DICOM download and viewer URLs
primary_issue: Pin both client and data release and record collection/data-use constraints; installed-wheel index version controls results (210-212).; Do not assume public equals unrestricted; retain collection-level terms and avoid re-identification/linkage attempts.; Optional BigQuery crosses into credentials/billing and is outside auth-free claims (339-355).; Printing PatientID and shareable viewer URLs requires output-handling review even for public data (173-198).

name: nnunet-segmentation
capability: nnU-Net v2 dataset conversion, planning, training, inference, ensembles and evaluation
primary_issue: Says nnU-Net automatically determines the optimal architecture and consistently achieves SOTA (11), which is not guaranteed for a new dataset.; A fixed 20-case threshold and production-pipeline recommendation (15-20,27) ignore task complexity, site shift, label quality and clinical validation.; The evaluation code names an average Hausdorff result hd95 and later reports 'Mean Avg HD', so metric semantics are inconsistent (348-403).; Example selects slices where prediction exists, which can hide false-negative slices and empty predictions in qualitative QC (425-431).; No patient-level/site-level split, leakage audit, external validation, uncertainty, calibration or clinical performance gate.

name: omero-integration
capability: OMERO image retrieval, annotations, ROIs and pipeline integration
primary_issue: Hard-codes password literals in multiple examples (43-45,67-73,94-96,318-319) rather than environment/secret-store use.; Creates and links tags/map annotations on the server (157-193,286-306) without preview, namespace governance, idempotency, permission review or readback.; TLS is optional and default listed false (342-350) despite sensitive image/credential transport.; No PHI, audit-log, least-privilege, group-context or data-export controls.

name: pathml
capability: PathML WSI tiling, stain normalization, nuclear masks, features and HDF5
primary_issue: Unpinned API examples plus 'upgrade pathml' troubleshooting (257-267) make behavior nonreproducible.; Exports tile coordinates and images without label/PHI screening (206-224).; Stain normalization and nuclear segmentation are presented without target provenance, QC criteria, tissue-type validation or domain-shift handling.; No patient/slide grouped split guidance; tile-level ML can leak patients across train/test.

name: pydicom-medical-imaging
capability: DICOM read/write, LUT/windowing, series volumes and purported anonymization
primary_issue: Quick start prints PatientName (47-52), normalizing disclosure of PHI.; The 'PS3.15 Annex E' anonymizer deletes only a short keyword list (257-282,538-570); it does not apply a DICOM confidentiality profile, private-tag policy, recursive sequence handling, date shifting, burned-in pixel review, overlays/graphics, free text, device IDs or referenced-UID remapping.; Single-file anonymize_dicom generates new Study/Series UIDs per call (270-278), breaking series/study relationships when used across files.; Changing SOPInstanceUID without synchronizing file_meta.MediaStorageSOPInstanceUID and references can produce internally inconsistent objects (275-277,564-567).; Sorting solely by ImagePositionPatient[2] assumes axial orientation and fails oblique/nonuniform geometry (611).

name: simpleitk-image-registration
capability: 3D I/O, registration, segmentation, filtering, resampling and conversion
primary_issue: Registration examples report optimizer metric but do not require visual overlay, landmarks, inverse consistency, Jacobian/folding checks or task performance (170-256).; Random metric sampling lacks a fixed seed, reducing reproducibility (213-239).; DICOM conversion should preserve/verify direction cosines, spacing and series selection and avoid PHI propagation.; Nearest-neighbor label resampling guidance is correct and explicit (786-815).

name: plannotate-plasmid-annotation
capability: Local BLAST-based circular plasmid feature annotation with GenBank/CSV/HTML export and batch CLI.
primary_issue: feature-database licensing; API/CLI unverified; verification overclaim; uncalibrated thresholds

name: sgrna-design-guide
declared_license: front matter open; body CC BY 4.0
capability: Select validated/Addgene or CRISPick guides and fall back to rule-based CRISPR guide design.
primary_issue: main code does not parse bundled data; dataset count/schema contradictions; actionable editing workflow lacks safety/ethics scope; scientific rules overgeneralized; data terms unresolved

name: viennarna-structure-prediction
capability: ViennaRNA MFE/partition/bpp/cofold/constraints/suboptimal structures, RNAfold CLI and RNA/guide accessibility recipes.
primary_issue: upstream license ambiguity; incorrect accessibility/guide inference; suspect API/index/energy handling; cellular-context limitations omitted

name: adaptyv-bio
capability: Submit protein sequences to a commercial cell-free expression/BLI service, poll jobs, retrieve KD/yield, and drive directed-evolution loops.
primary_issue: unverified SDK/API contract; external paid mutation without explicit confirmation and spend gate; no sequence privacy/IP or acceptable-use handling; no biosafety/design screening

name: esm-protein-language-model
capability: Local/cloud ESM3 generation, structure prediction and inverse folding, plus ESM C embeddings.
primary_issue: API examples are version-sensitive and unverified; model/weight/service licensing unresolved; no sequence safety/privacy screen; no wet-lab validation contract

name: hmdb-database
capability: Parse a registered local HMDB XML export for metabolites, properties, disease/context links, spectra and cross-references.
primary_issue: bulk-data terms unresolved; schema/release unpinned; clinical and mass-ID overclaim

name: interpro-database
capability: InterPro REST queries for entries, protein domain architecture, members, taxonomy and PDB links.
primary_issue: endpoint behavior unverified; release unpinned; member-data attribution incomplete

name: matchms-spectral-matching
capability: Spectrum I/O/filtering, cosine/modified-cosine/fingerprint scoring and library search.
primary_issue: unverified/version-sensitive API; compound-identification overclaim; no spectral-library provenance or FDR

name: maxquant-proteomics
capability: Configure/run MaxQuant and perform LFQ/SILAC filtering, normalization, imputation, t-tests, volcano plots and enrichment.
primary_issue: upstream license mismatch; statistically unsafe default pipeline; no experimental-design contract; unverified MaxQuant schema/version

name: metabolomics-workbench-database
capability: Metabolomics Workbench REST queries for compounds, RefMet names, m/z candidates, studies and gene/protein annotations.
primary_issue: live contract unverified; terms/license unresolved; metabolite-ID and cross-study boundaries incomplete

name: pride-database
capability: PRIDE v3 project/facet/file/protein-occurrence search and generation of bulk download manifests.
primary_issue: registry contradiction; API unverified; depositor-file rights and human-data handling absent; bulk-download gate absent

name: pyopenms-mass-spectrometry
capability: OpenMS bindings for MS I/O, signal/feature processing, peptide/protein IDs, metabolomics and format conversion.
primary_issue: incorrect FDR semantics; incomplete alignment code; unverified API signatures; insufficient experimental QC/identification contract

name: uniprot-protein-database
capability: UniProt REST search, FASTA, ID mapping, field selection and bulk streaming.
primary_issue: async mapping incomplete; release unpinned; mapping ambiguity under-specified

name: aeon
capability: time-series classification/regression; clustering; segmentation; transformations; UCR/UEA benchmarking
primary_issue: Useful candidate, but benchmark claims such as MiniROCKET ~75x and k=1 often best are context-specific. Dataset loaders imply network retrieval; evaluation examples need grouped/temporal split guidance where applicable.

name: astropy-astronomy
capability: units/constants; coordinates/time/cosmology; FITS/Table/WCS; modeling; visualization; SAMP
primary_issue: Broad, generally sound candidate. Planck18 is called the current standard too categorically; cosmology must match study convention. FITS verify('fix') can silently mutate metadata and remote/SAMP capabilities need trust boundaries.

name: dask-parallel-computing
capability: dataframe/array/bag; delayed/futures; distributed scheduler; SLURM/Kubernetes; Dask-ML
primary_issue: Valuable infrastructure knowledge, but distributed Dask transports serialized Python objects and exposes dashboards/schedulers; the guide lacks authentication/TLS/untrusted-worker warnings. Generic normalization code can cause leakage if applied before split.

name: degenerate-input-filtering
capability: constant/all-NaN/empty input checks; sequence/file checks; filter logging
primary_issue: The reporting idea is useful, but claims that zero variance makes t-tests and fold-change undefined are false in general, scipy ttest behavior is mischaracterized, and generic gene/event/batch thresholds can remove scientifically valid signals or induce selection bias. Filtering must be analysis-specific and prespecified.

name: exploratory-data-analysis
capability: format classification; integrity/schema/missingness checks; domain QC routing; provenance reporting
primary_issue: Good intake checklist but too broad to be executable safely. It tells agents to install missing libraries and suggest normalization/imputation before experimental-design context is established. Vendor/clinical/genomic formats need dedicated validators.

name: geopandas-geospatial
capability: vector I/O; CRS transforms; spatial joins/overlays; geometry operations; choropleths; PostGIS
primary_issue: CRS warnings are valuable. Basemap/database/remote-file examples need network and credential controls; area/distance accuracy needs explicit projection selection and geometry validity repair provenance.

name: hypogenic-hypothesis-generation
capability: LLM hypothesis generation; literature refinement; validation-loop ranking; multi-hypothesis inference
primary_issue: High-risk automation: it repeatedly optimizes hypotheses against a validation set, which encourages adaptive overfitting and does not constitute scientific hypothesis testing. The quick start/API surface is unversioned; prompts may exfiltrate sensitive observations. No multiplicity, preregistration, independent replication or uncertainty contract.

name: matlab-scientific-computing
declared_license: GPL-3.0 (GNU Octave); MATLAB requires commercial license
capability: matrix/numerical computing; optimization/ODE/signal/image; MATLAB-Octave interoperability; CLI execution
primary_issue: Broad code cookbook. sudo apt install and direct MATLAB/Octave execution exceed safe skill behavior. MATLAB and Octave are not drop-in equivalent; examples require runtime-specific validation and toolbox license detection.

name: nan-safe-correlation
capability: NaN summaries; pairwise-complete Spearman; degenerate-feature filtering; effective-n reporting
primary_issue: Pairwise n reporting is valuable, but it asserts bulk rank/corr is incorrect, uses arbitrary min_valid/50% thresholds, filters nunique<3 (excluding valid binary features), and omits multiple-testing correction and missingness-mechanism caveats. Pairwise deletion can yield non-positive-semidefinite correlation matrices and noncomparable n.

name: neb-irc-activation-energy
capability: GFN2-xTB endpoint optimization; CI-NEB; TS optimization/Hessian; IRC checks; barrier reporting; profile plotting
primary_issue: Reject. Installer downloads and extracts an unverified tarball and uses pip --break-system-packages. The purported mandatory third NEB gate becomes WARN and exit-success when trajectory is absent. Absence of a >2 kJ/mol interior well does not prove a single barrier. IRC plotting uses unaligned coordinate RMSD and selects the highest sampled frame as TS, so orientation/barrier can be wrong. No method uncertainty or electronic-structure adequacy gate can make xTB barriers quantitative.

name: networkx-graph-analysis
capability: graph construction/I-O; centrality/paths/components; community algorithms; generators; visualization
primary_issue: Good general candidate. GraphML/GEXF are safer than pickle; any gpickle or arbitrary object-node serialization must be excluded. Algorithmic results depend on directedness, weights, disconnectedness, random seeds and resolution, which need stronger reporting.

name: neurokit2
capability: ECG/EDA/EMG/PPG/RSP processing; event-related and interval features; HRV; simulation
primary_issue: Potentially valuable but biomedical signal pipelines need sampling-rate/device/artifact validation and cannot be treated as clinical interpretation. Default automated cleaning and HRV on short/noisy segments need modality-specific minimums and provenance.

name: neuropixels-analysis
capability: Neuropixels loading/preprocessing; Kilosort4; quality metrics; PSTH/tuning/decoding; NWB export
primary_issue: Reject as operational recipe. It states questionable fixed channel counts/hardware requirements, duplicates the SpikeInterface skill, uses destructive remove_existing_folder=True, and relies on pre-0.101 extract_waveforms APIs while the sibling advertises SortingAnalyzer. QC thresholds are not ground-truth validation.

name: nextflow-workflow-engine
capability: DSL2 processes/workflows; channels/operators; containers/conda; executors; nf-core; reports/resume
primary_issue: Workflow concepts are useful, but curl|bash remote-code execution, unpinned nf-core pipelines/containers, cloud/HPC executors and arbitrary process scripts are outside a safe general skill. Reproducibility requires immutable revision/container digests and explicit data egress policy.

name: polars-dataframes
capability: eager/lazy frames; expressions; joins/windows; streaming; I/O/cloud/database; pandas migration
primary_issue: Strong data-engineering candidate, but ancillary examples assign cloud secrets in process environment and include remote database/cloud writes without approval boundaries. Version-sensitive streaming/Excel/cloud APIs and performance claims need pins and fixtures.

name: pyhealth
capability: MIMIC/eICU/OMOP ingestion; code mappings; clinical prediction tasks; deep models; metrics
primary_issue: Reject without clinical-data governance. It handles credentialed patient-level EHR but has no PHI/de-identification, DUA, secure storage, cohort leakage, temporal split, external validation, calibration, fairness, or clinical-use disclaimer. A patient split alone does not prevent temporal or site leakage.

name: pymatgen
capability: structures/compositions; phase diagrams; Materials Project queries; electronic/XRD analysis; VASP input; format conversion
primary_issue: Core local structure operations are promising. Credential examples encourage embedding a key in a Python command/SETTINGS and falling back to the literal your_key. Materials Project schemas and VASP defaults are version/pseudopotential sensitive; generated inputs are not scientifically validated calculations.

name: pymoo
capability: single/multiobjective optimization; constraints; NSGA-II/III/MOEA-D; indicators; visualization
primary_issue: Useful candidate. Optimization output is stochastic and depends on scaling, constraint formulation, termination and seed; examples need repeated-run uncertainty and held-out objective evaluation where simulators/data-driven surrogates are involved.

name: scikit-learn-machine-learning
capability: preprocessing/pipelines; classification/regression; CV/tuning; metrics; persistence
primary_issue: Core pipeline guidance is reusable, but joblib.load is arbitrary code execution for untrusted files and is shown without warning. name: shap-model-explainability

primary_issue: SHAP values explain a fitted model under a background/conditionality convention, not causality or feature truth. The skill needs correlated-feature, data-leakage and background-distribution guardrails. joblib.load of an explainer is unsafe for untrusted artifacts.

name: simpy-discrete-event-simulation
capability: processes/events; resources/stores/containers; interrupts; monitoring; replications
primary_issue: Strong conceptual candidate. Simulation conclusions require warm-up/burn-in, independent replications, uncertainty intervals, seed streams, verification/validation against real systems and sensitivity analysis; cookbook output alone is not evidence.

name: snakemake-workflow-engine
capability: rules/DAG; wildcards/config; conda/containers; cluster profiles; reports/benchmarking
primary_issue: Reject as unrestricted skill: Snakemake rules execute arbitrary shell, remote downloads and cluster submissions. The example embeds wget in a rule and production submission commands. Dry-run validates the DAG, not shell safety, data provenance or scientific correctness.

name: spikeinterface-electrophysiology
capability: 20+ readers; preprocessing; sorter orchestration; SortingAnalyzer/QC; sorter comparison; NWB/Phy export
primary_issue: Static reference has value, but containerized sorters and external binaries are arbitrary code execution. name: sympy-symbolic-math
capability: exact algebra/calculus; equation/ODE solving; symbolic matrices; code generation; physics
primary_issue: Good candidate. Generated C/Fortran and lambdified expressions need explicit symbol assumptions, domain/singularity checks, numerical verification and no automatic compilation/execution. Solver output can be conditional/incomplete.

name: torch-geometric-graph-neural-networks
capability: homogeneous/heterogeneous graph data; GNN layers/message passing; pooling; neighbor sampling; explainability; datasets
primary_issue: Promising reference, but graph splits must prevent edge/node/scaffold/temporal leakage according to task. Dataset downloads and PyTorch checkpoints are external/untrusted artifacts. Accuracy examples lack repeated seeds and baselines.

name: transformers-bio-nlp
capability: biomedical NER/classification/QA/generation; embeddings/search; fine-tuning
primary_issue: Reject as-is. from_pretrained downloads mutable third-party code/weights; model licenses vary. Performance claims (5-15%, under an hour) lack matched benchmarks/hardware. Generated biomedical statements and naive drug-disease pair extraction can fabricate evidence; model output must never be treated as literature fact.

name: umap-learn
capability: standard/supervised/parametric UMAP; DensMAP/AlignedUMAP; transform/inverse; custom metrics; clustering/classification workflows
primary_issue: Contains overclaims that UMAP preserves global structure and that features must always be standardized. Scaling is metric/data dependent. name: uspto-database

primary_issue: Reject because every REST example targets the legacy api.patentsview.org query surface and rate/auth claims are time-sensitive with no retrieval date. Patent keyword/assignee counts are not prior-art or freedom-to-operate conclusions; legal interpretation guardrails are absent.

name: vaex-dataframes
capability: out-of-core frames; virtual columns; aggregation/binning; cloud I/O; ML transforms; server

name: citation-management

The skill repeatedly says FDA-approved/authoritative and recommends EHR integration without regulatory/clinical validation. The example UUID is explicitly synthetic and cannot demonstrate warning lookup. No effective-date/current-label reconciliation.

Scaffold split alone does not validate prospective utility. Models/datasets lack cards, licenses, leakage checks, applicability domains, uncertainty and calibration.

name: diffdock
capability: Blind protein-ligand pose generation with DiffDock, preprocessing, inference subprocess, confidence parsing, residue contacts, visualization and Vina rescoring.
primary_issue: No repo tag/commit/model release/checksum/license for code or weights. Confidence >0 is presented as generally plausible without calibration by model release/complex type. Confidence ranks poses, not affinity; standard DiffDock is unsuitable for hit ranking without separate validation. PDB cleanup removes heteroatoms/cofactors and gap-filling advice can alter the site. Unrelated PatentsView citation signals poor provenance control.

name: drugbank-database-access
capability: Local DrugBank XML parsing for drug metadata, interactions, targets/pathways, chemical properties, similarity and polypharmacy reports.
primary_issue: Major clinical overclaim: DrugBank interaction prose is converted to major/moderate/minor by substring and summed with arbitrary 10/3/1 weights. 'increase/decrease' is not severity. Account/database is licensed and versioned but snapshot version/date are absent. ADMET heuristics and chemical-property preference are not predictions fit for decisions.

name: emdb-database
capability: EMDB keyword search, entry/map metadata, fitted PDB cross-references, sample/organism and citation extraction through EBI APIs.
primary_issue: Nested schema is brittle and no API version/date is pinned. Resolution/method metadata must not be treated as map quality or atomic-model validation. Download URL/schema requires live official verification before implementation.

name: fda-database
capability: openFDA FAERS, label, NDC and enforcement searches, counts, label extraction, safety comparisons and approval-status recipe.
primary_issue: FAERS counts cannot compare incidence or differentiated safety without exposure, deduplication, case definitions and disproportionality methods. Although line 380 warns counts are not incidence, workflow still labels raw top counts a safety comparison. openFDA label presence/application_number does not by itself prove NDA/ANDA approval or approval year; the recipe does not output a year.

name: gtopdb-database
capability: GtoPdb target/ligand/family metadata, cross-references, structures, quantitative interactions and approved-ligand queries.
primary_issue: pKi/pIC50/pKd/pEC50 are not interchangeable; numeric coercion deliberately drops ranges/qualifiers and must not silently bias ranking. Approved flag source/jurisdiction/date needs preservation. API behaviors are asserted from live verification but not versioned.

name: mdanalysis-trajectory
capability: Local MD trajectory I/O/selections, RMSD/RMSF, hydrogen bonds, PCA/clustering, contacts and representative-frame extraction.
primary_issue: 'Binding stability' from RMSD/contact/H-bonds is descriptive trajectory behavior, not affinity or residence time. Hard-coded version output is not a pin. Periodic-boundary alignment, topology, units, equilibration, sampling and replicate convergence must be explicit.

name: mdtraj-trajectory-analysis
capability: Local MDTraj trajectory I/O, RMSD/Rg/RMSF, contacts, torsions, DSSP, hydrogen bonds, SASA and replicate summaries.
primary_issue: Descriptive stability/flexibility metrics cannot infer affinity. DSSP availability and SHIFTX2 external execution/licensing are not fully specified. Version unpinned; PBC/alignment/replicate convergence controls need explicit contracts.

name: medchem
capability: Local drug/lead/fragment/CNS rules, PAINS/common/NIBR/Lilly alerts, groups, catalogs, complexity and property constraints.

Association score is evidence aggregation, not causal validity or target suitability. Safety/tractability require source-level interpretation.

name: pdb-database
capability: RCSB Search API text/attribute/sequence/3D similarity, Data API GraphQL, coordinate/FASTA downloads, pagination/batching and Bio.PDB parsing.

API attribute/schema behavior is unversioned. Entry-level metadata must preserve revision/experimental method/resolution and assembly choice.
